records.literal_gloss: And came Gideon, and look, a man [was] recounting to his companion a dream, and he said, look, a dream I dreamed, and look, a round loaf of bread of barley tumbling into [the] camp of Midian, and it came to the tent and struck it, and it fell, and turned it upward, and fell the tent.

en.L: And Gideon came, and look, a man [was] telling a dream to his companion, and he said, "Look, I dreamed a dream, and look, a round loaf of barley bread [was] tumbling into the camp of Midian; and it came to the tent and struck it, and it fell, and it turned it upside down, and the tent lay flat."
en.B: Just as Gideon arrived, one man was describing a dream to his friend. "Listen," he said, "I had a dream. A round loaf of barley bread came rolling into the camp of Midian. It came to the tent and hit it so hard that it fell. It turned the tent upside down, and the tent collapsed."
en.R: When Gideon got there, he heard a man telling his friend about a dream. The man said, "In my dream I saw a round loaf of barley bread roll into the Midianite camp. It hit the tent so hard that the tent turned over and fell flat."

sw.L: Naye Gideoni akaja, na tazama, mtu [alikuwa] akimsimulia mwenzake ndoto, akasema, "Tazama, niliota ndoto, na tazama, mkate wa duara wa shayiri [ulikuwa] ukiviringika kuingia kambini mwa Midiani; ukafika kwenye hema, ukaipiga, nayo ikaanguka, ukaipindua juu chini, nayo hema ikalala chini."
sw.B: Gideoni alipofika, mtu mmoja alikuwa akimsimulia rafiki yake ndoto. Akasema, "Sikiliza, niliota ndoto. Mkate wa duara wa shayiri ulikuja ukiviringika mpaka kambini mwa Midiani. Ukafika kwenye hema, ukaipiga kwa nguvu hata ikaanguka. Ukaipindua hema juu chini, nayo ikaporomoka."
sw.R: Gideoni alipofika huko, alimsikia mtu mmoja akimsimulia rafiki yake ndoto. Mtu huyo alisema, "Katika ndoto yangu niliona mkate wa duara wa shayiri ukiviringika kuingia kambini mwa Wamidiani. Ukaipiga hema kwa nguvu sana hata hema ikapinduka na kuanguka chini kabisa."

es.L: Y llegó Gedeón, y he aquí, un hombre contaba un sueño a su compañero, y decía: «Mira, soñé un sueño, y he aquí, un pan redondo de cebada rodaba hasta el campamento de Madián; y llegó a la tienda y la golpeó, y cayó, y la volcó de arriba abajo, y la tienda quedó en el suelo.»
es.B: Justo cuando llegó Gedeón, un hombre le estaba contando un sueño a su amigo. «Escucha», le decía, «tuve un sueño. Un pan redondo de cebada venía rodando hasta el campamento de Madián. Llegó a la tienda y la golpeó con tanta fuerza que cayó. La volcó de arriba abajo, y la tienda se vino al suelo.»
es.R: Cuando Gedeón llegó, oyó a un hombre que le contaba un sueño a su amigo. El hombre decía: «En mi sueño vi un pan redondo de cebada que rodaba hasta el campamento madianita. Golpeó la tienda con tanta fuerza que la tienda se volcó y cayó al suelo.»

decisions.choice: a round loaf: the read form of a rare word
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the Hebrew text and the form handed down for reading differ slightly in this word; the pinned data follows the read form. The word comes only here, and its sense is taken from a root meaning "to roll" or "to be round": a round, flat loaf or cake. Reviewers should check this against the manuscript notes.

decisions.choice: barley bread: plain food of farmers
decisions.reason: Barley was cheaper than wheat and was the bread of ordinary and poorer people (2 Kings 4:42; John 6:9). A loaf of farmers' bread knocking over a tent of the desert raiders is a picture of Israel, the people of the field, overturning Midian, the people of tents. Verse 14 gives the friend's reading of it.

decisions.choice: the tent: probably a particular tent, perhaps the leader's
decisions.reason: The word has the article, "the tent", as if one tent stood out in the camp, perhaps the commander's. It may simply mean the tent seen in the dream. "Turned it upward" means turned it upside down, and the last clause sums up: the tent lay flat.

decisions.choice: Listen (Balanced); left out (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "look" three times, drawing attention to what is seen and told. Literal keeps it each time; Balanced uses "Listen" once at the start of the dream, and Readable lets "he heard" and "I saw" carry the sense.

source.text: וַיַּ֨עַן רֵעֵ֤הוּ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֵ֣ין זֹ֔את בִּלְתִּ֗י אִם־חֶ֛רֶב גִּדְע֥וֹן בֶּן־יוֹאָ֖שׁ אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל נָתַ֤ן הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ בְּיָד֔וֹ אֶת־מִדְיָ֖ן וְאֶת־כָּל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And answered his companion and said, not [is] this except [the] sword of Gideon son of Joash, a man of Israel; has given God into his hand Midian and all the camp.

en.L: And his companion answered and said, "This [is] nothing except the sword of Gideon son of Joash, a man of Israel. God has given Midian and all the camp into his hand."
en.B: His friend replied, "This can be nothing but the sword of Gideon son of Joash, the Israelite! God has handed Midian and the whole army over to him."
en.R: His friend answered, "This must mean the sword of Gideon son of Joash, the Israelite. God has given him victory over Midian and our whole army."

sw.L: Naye mwenzake akajibu, akasema, "Hili [si] kitu kingine ila upanga wa Gideoni mwana wa Yoashi, mtu wa Israeli. Mungu amewatia Midiani na kambi yote mkononi mwake."
sw.B: Rafiki yake akajibu, "Hii haiwezi kuwa kitu kingine ila upanga wa Gideoni mwana wa Yoashi, yule Mwisraeli! Mungu amewatia Midiani na jeshi lote mikononi mwake."
sw.R: Rafiki yake akajibu, "Hii lazima ina maana ya upanga wa Gideoni mwana wa Yoashi, yule Mwisraeli. Mungu amempa ushindi juu ya Midiani na jeshi letu lote."

es.L: Y su compañero respondió y dijo: «Esto no [es] otra cosa sino la espada de Gedeón hijo de Joás, hombre de Israel. Dios ha entregado en su mano a Madián y a todo el campamento.»
es.B: Su amigo le respondió: «¡Esto no puede ser otra cosa que la espada de Gedeón hijo de Joás, el israelita! Dios le ha entregado a Madián y a todo el ejército.»
es.R: Su amigo le respondió: «Esto tiene que ser la espada de Gedeón hijo de Joás, el israelita. Dios le ha dado la victoria sobre Madián y sobre todo nuestro ejército.»

decisions.choice: God: a Midianite speaks of Israel's God
decisions.reason: The man uses the general word for God, not the LORD's personal name. The enemy himself admits that Israel's God has decided the battle (compare Rahab in Joshua 2:9-11). When Gideon answers in verse 15, he names the LORD.

decisions.choice: has given: spoken as already done
decisions.reason: As in verse 9, the past form treats the coming defeat as certain. The LORD's promise to Gideon is echoed by an enemy's mouth.

decisions.choice: the sword of Gideon: picked up in the battle cry
decisions.reason: The dream is read as Gideon's sword, and in verse 20 Gideon's men will cry "A sword for the LORD and for Gideon!".

decisions.choice: all the camp: the whole army in the camp
decisions.reason: The word for "camp" also means those who are camped there, the army (verses 21-22).

decisions.choice: our whole army
decisions.reason: The speaker is one of the Midianite soldiers; Readable adds "our" to make that clear.

source.text: וַיְהִי֩ כִשְׁמֹ֨עַ גִּדְע֜וֹן אֶת־מִסְפַּ֧ר הַחֲל֛וֹם וְאֶת־שִׁבְר֖וֹ וַיִּשְׁתָּ֑חוּ וַיָּ֨שָׁב֙ אֶל־מַחֲנֵ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ק֔וּמוּ כִּֽי־נָתַ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה בְּיֶדְכֶ֖ם אֶת־מַחֲנֵ֥ה מִדְיָֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when heard Gideon the recounting of the dream and its breaking, and he bowed down; and he returned to [the] camp of Israel and said, arise, for has given Yahweh into your hand [the] camp of Midian.

en.L: And it happened, when Gideon heard the telling of the dream and its interpretation, that he bowed down; and he returned to the camp of Israel and said, "Arise, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given the camp of Midian into your hand."
en.B: When Gideon heard the dream and what it meant, he bowed down in worship. Then he went back to the camp of Israel and called out, "Get up! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has handed the camp of Midian over to you."
en.R: When Gideon heard about the dream and what it meant, he bowed down to worship. Then he went back to the Israelite camp and shouted, "Get up! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has given you victory over the Midianite army!"

sw.L: Ikawa Gideoni aliposikia masimulizi ya ndoto na tafsiri yake, akasujudu; akarudi kambini mwa Israeli, akasema, "Inukeni, kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameitia kambi ya Midiani mkononi mwenu."
sw.B: Gideoni aliposikia ndoto hiyo na maana yake, alisujudu na kuabudu. Kisha akarudi kambini mwa Israeli, akaita, "Amkeni! {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameitia kambi ya Midiani mikononi mwenu."
sw.R: Gideoni aliposikia habari ya ndoto na maana yake, alisujudu ili kuabudu. Kisha akarudi kambini mwa Waisraeli, akapaza sauti, "Amkeni! {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amewapa ushindi juu ya jeshi la Wamidiani!"

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando Gedeón oyó el relato del sueño y su interpretación, se postró; y volvió al campamento de Israel y dijo: «{{plural_you:Levántense|Levantaos}}, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha entregado en {{plural_you:su mano|vuestra mano}} el campamento de Madián.»
es.B: Cuando Gedeón oyó el sueño y lo que significaba, se postró en adoración. Luego volvió al campamento de Israel y gritó: «¡{{plural_you:Levántense|Levantaos}}! {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:les|os}} ha entregado el campamento de Madián.»
es.R: Cuando Gedeón oyó el sueño y lo que significaba, se inclinó para adorar. Luego volvió al campamento israelita y gritó: «¡{{plural_you:Levántense|Levantaos}}! ¡{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:les|os}} ha dado la victoria sobre el ejército madianita!»

decisions.choice: its interpretation: literally "its breaking", a word that points to the breaking of the jars
decisions.reason: The usual word for "breaking" is used here, uniquely, for the meaning of a dream: what it breaks open, its solution. The same idea of breaking returns when the men smash their jars (verses 19-20).

decisions.choice: he bowed down: in worship
decisions.reason: The verb means to bow low before someone; with no one else named, it is worship of the LORD, who had sent him to hear the dream (as in Genesis 24:26; Exodus 4:31).

decisions.choice: the LORD has given: the same certainty as in verses 9 and 14
decisions.reason: Gideon now says to his men what the LORD said to him (verse 9) and what the Midianite said (verse 14), using the LORD's name.

decisions.choice: the Midianite army
decisions.reason: "The camp of Midian" here is the army camped there (verse 14); Readable says "army".

source.text: וַיַּ֛חַץ אֶת־שְׁלֹשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת הָאִ֖ישׁ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה רָאשִׁ֑ים וַיִּתֵּ֨ן שׁוֹפָר֤וֹת בְּיַד־כֻּלָּם֙ וְכַדִּ֣ים רֵקִ֔ים וְלַפִּדִ֖ים בְּת֥וֹךְ הַכַּדִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And he divided the three hundred men [into] three companies, and he put trumpets in [the] hand of all of them, and jars empty, and torches inside the jars.

en.L: And he divided the 300 men [into] three companies, and he put trumpets in the hand of all of them, and empty jars, with torches inside the jars.
en.B: He divided the 300 men into three companies and gave each of them a ram's horn and an empty jar, with a torch inside the jar.
en.R: Gideon divided the 300 men into three groups. He gave each man a trumpet and an empty clay jar with a burning torch inside it.

sw.L: Naye akawagawa wale watu mia tatu [katika] vikosi vitatu, akatia baragumu mkononi mwa wote, na mitungi mitupu, na mienge ndani ya mitungi.
sw.B: Aliwagawa wale watu mia tatu katika vikosi vitatu, akampa kila mmoja baragumu na mtungi mtupu, na mwenge ndani ya mtungi.
sw.R: Gideoni aliwagawa wale watu mia tatu katika makundi matatu. Alimpa kila mtu baragumu na mtungi mtupu wa udongo wenye mwenge unaowaka ndani yake.

es.L: Y dividió a los trescientos hombres [en] tres compañías, y puso cuernos en la mano de todos ellos, y cántaros vacíos, con antorchas dentro de los cántaros.
es.B: Dividió a los trescientos hombres en tres compañías y les dio a todos un cuerno de carnero y un cántaro vacío, con una antorcha dentro del cántaro.
es.R: Gedeón dividió a los trescientos hombres en tres grupos. A cada hombre le dio un cuerno de carnero y un cántaro vacío de barro con una antorcha encendida adentro.

decisions.choice: companies: literally "heads"
decisions.reason: "Heads" is used for divisions of an army, each with its own leader (9:34, 43; 1 Samuel 11:11; 13:17).

decisions.choice: torches inside empty jars: lights hidden until the signal
decisions.reason: The jars were pottery jars, the kind used for carrying water (Genesis 24:14). A lit torch inside a jar could be carried at night without being seen, and shown all at once when the jar was broken (verse 20).

decisions.choice: trumpets: rams' horns, one for each man
decisions.reason: As in verse 8, the shofar is a ram's horn. Normally only a few men in an army would blow horns, so 300 horns at once would sound like a very large force.

decisions.choice: clay; burning
decisions.reason: Readable adds that the jars were clay, which is why they could be smashed, and that the torches were burning, which the Hebrew takes for granted (verse 20).

decisions.choice: "cuernos" (L), "cuerno de carnero" (B, R) for the shofars; "cántaros" for the jars
alternatives: "trompetas", as the English Literal and Readable
decisions.reason: As for 3:27, the shofar is a ram's horn (m3). Literal says "cuernos", keeping one plain word for the Hebrew one, and Balanced and Readable name the animal; "trompeta" would suggest a metal instrument.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם מִמֶּ֥נִּי תִרְא֖וּ וְכֵ֣ן תַּעֲשׂ֑וּ וְהִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֥י בָא֙ בִּקְצֵ֣ה הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וְהָיָ֥ה כַאֲשֶׁר־אֶעֱשֶׂ֖ה כֵּ֥ן תַּעֲשֽׂוּן׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, from me you will see, and thus you will do; and look, I [am] coming into [the] edge of the camp, and it will be, as I do, so you will do.

en.L: And he said to them, "Look at me, and do likewise. And look, [when] I come to the edge of the camp, then it shall be: as I do, so you shall do.
en.B: "Watch me," he told them, "and do what I do. When I reach the edge of the camp, do exactly as I do.
en.R: He told them, "Watch me and do what I do. When I get to the edge of the camp, do just what I do.

sw.L: Naye akawaambia, "Niangalieni mimi, mkafanye vivyo hivyo. Na tazama, [nitakapofika] ukingoni mwa kambi, itakuwa hivi: kama nitakavyofanya, ndivyo mtakavyofanya.
sw.B: Akawaambia, "Niangalieni, mfanye kama nifanyavyo. Nikifika ukingoni mwa kambi, fanyeni sawasawa na ninavyofanya.
sw.R: Aliwaambia, "Niangalieni, mfanye kama ninavyofanya. Nikifika ukingoni mwa kambi, fanyeni kama ninavyofanya mimi.

es.L: Y les dijo: «{{plural_you:Mírenme|Miradme}} a mí, y {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} lo mismo. Y he aquí, [cuando] yo llegue al extremo del campamento, será que como yo haga, así {{plural_you:harán|haréis}} {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: «{{plural_you:Mírenme|Miradme}}», les dijo, «y {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} lo que yo haga. Cuando llegue al borde del campamento, {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} exactamente lo que yo haga.
es.R: Les dijo: «{{plural_you:Mírenme|Miradme}} y {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} lo que yo haga. Cuando llegue al borde del campamento, {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} lo mismo que yo.

decisions.choice: from me you will see: watch me and take your lead from me
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "from me you will see", meaning "learn from what I do". Gideon's men are to copy his signals exactly.

decisions.choice: look, I am coming: when I come
decisions.reason: "Look" with a participle points to what is about to happen; here it sets the time for the command that follows.

source.text: וְתָקַעְתִּי֙ בַּשּׁוֹפָ֔ר אָנֹכִ֖י וְכָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתִּ֑י וּתְקַעְתֶּ֨ם בַּשּׁוֹפָר֜וֹת גַּם־אַתֶּ֗ם סְבִיבוֹת֙ כָּל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֖ם לַיהוָ֥ה וּלְגִדְעֽוֹן׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And I will blow on the trumpet, I and all who [are] with me, and you will blow on the trumpets, also you, all around all the camp, and you will say, for Yahweh and for Gideon.

en.L: And [when] I blow on the trumpet, I and all who [are] with me, then you also shall blow on the trumpets all around the whole camp, and you shall say, 'For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and for Gideon!'"
en.B: When I blow my horn, along with everyone who is with me, you are to blow your horns too, on every side of the camp, and shout, 'For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and for Gideon!'"
en.R: When my group and I blow our trumpets, all of you on every side of the camp must blow your trumpets too. Then shout, 'For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and for Gideon!'"

sw.L: Nami [nitakapopiga] baragumu, mimi na wote [walio] pamoja nami, ndipo nanyi pia mtapiga baragumu pande zote za kambi nzima, na kusema, 'Kwa ajili ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na kwa ajili ya Gideoni!'"
sw.B: Nitakapopiga baragumu yangu, pamoja na wote walio pamoja nami, nanyi pia mpige baragumu zenu pande zote za kambi, mkipiga kelele, 'Kwa ajili ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na kwa ajili ya Gideoni!'"
sw.R: Mimi na kundi langu tutakapopiga baragumu zetu, ninyi nyote mlio pande zote za kambi lazima mpige baragumu zenu pia. Kisha pigeni kelele, 'Kwa ajili ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na kwa ajili ya Gideoni!'"

es.L: Y [cuando] yo toque el cuerno, yo y todos los que [están] conmigo, entonces también {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:tocarán|tocaréis}} los cuernos alrededor de todo el campamento, y {{plural_you:dirán|diréis}}: “¡Por {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} y por Gedeón!”»
es.B: Cuando yo toque mi cuerno, junto con todos los que están conmigo, {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} también {{plural_you:toquen|tocad}} sus cuernos por todos los lados del campamento y {{plural_you:griten|gritad}}: “¡Por {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} y por Gedeón!”»
es.R: Cuando mi grupo y yo toquemos los cuernos, todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, por todos los lados del campamento, {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} que tocar también los cuernos. Luego {{plural_you:griten|gritad}}: “¡Por {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} y por Gedeón!”»

decisions.choice: For the LORD and for Gideon: a short battle cry
decisions.reason: The cry names the one the battle is fought for and the leader he has chosen. When the men actually shout it in verse 20, they say it in a fuller form: "A sword for the LORD and for Gideon!"

decisions.choice: all around the whole camp: the three companies surround the camp
decisions.reason: With 100 men in each company (verses 16, 19), Gideon's force is spread around the camp so that the noise and lights come from every side.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֣א גִ֠דְעוֹן וּמֵאָה־אִ֨ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־אִתּ֜וֹ בִּקְצֵ֣ה הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֗ה רֹ֚אשׁ הָאַשְׁמֹ֣רֶת הַתִּֽיכוֹנָ֔ה אַ֛ךְ הָקֵ֥ם הֵקִ֖ימוּ אֶת־הַשֹּֽׁמְרִ֑ים וַֽיִּתְקְעוּ֙ בַּשּׁ֣וֹפָר֔וֹת וְנָפ֥וֹץ הַכַּדִּ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּיָדָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And came Gideon and [the] hundred men who [were] with him to [the] edge of the camp [at the] beginning of the watch, the middle; only establishing they had established the watchmen; and they blew on the trumpets, and smashing the jars which [were] in their hand.

en.L: And Gideon and the 100 men who [were] with him came to the edge of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch, when they had just posted the watchmen; and they blew on the trumpets and smashed the jars that [were] in their hand.
en.B: Gideon and the 100 men with him reached the edge of the camp at the start of the middle watch of the night, just after the new guards had been posted. They blew their horns and smashed the jars they were holding.
en.R: Gideon and his 100 men reached the edge of the camp in the middle of the night, at the start of the second watch, just after the Midianites had changed guards. The men blew their trumpets and smashed the jars they were carrying.

sw.L: Naye Gideoni na wale watu mia [waliokuwa] pamoja naye wakafika ukingoni mwa kambi mwanzoni mwa zamu ya kati ya walinzi, walipokuwa wamewaweka walinzi hivi punde; nao wakapiga baragumu, wakaivunja mitungi [iliyokuwa] mikononi mwao.
sw.B: Gideoni na watu mia waliokuwa pamoja naye walifika ukingoni mwa kambi mwanzoni mwa zamu ya kati ya usiku, mara tu baada ya walinzi wapya kuwekwa. Walipiga baragumu zao, wakaivunja mitungi waliyokuwa wameishika.
sw.R: Gideoni na watu wake mia walifika ukingoni mwa kambi katikati ya usiku, mwanzoni mwa zamu ya pili ya ulinzi, mara tu baada ya Wamidiani kubadilisha walinzi. Watu hao walipiga baragumu zao, wakaivunja mitungi waliyokuwa wamebeba.

es.L: Y llegó Gedeón con los cien hombres que [estaban] con él al extremo del campamento al comienzo de la vigilia de la medianoche, cuando acababan de poner a los centinelas; y tocaron los cuernos y rompieron los cántaros que [tenían] en su mano.
es.B: Gedeón y los cien hombres que iban con él llegaron al borde del campamento al comienzo de la vigilia de la medianoche, justo después de que habían puesto a los nuevos centinelas. Tocaron sus cuernos y rompieron los cántaros que llevaban.
es.R: Gedeón y sus cien hombres llegaron al borde del campamento en medio de la noche, al comienzo de la segunda vigilia, justo después de que los madianitas habían cambiado la guardia. Los hombres tocaron sus cuernos y rompieron los cántaros que llevaban.

decisions.choice: the beginning of the middle watch: some hours after dark
decisions.reason: Israel divided the night into three watches (Lamentations 2:19 speaks of the beginning of the watches; Exodus 14:24 and 1 Samuel 11:11 of the morning watch). The middle watch ran through the middle of the night, from about late evening to the small hours. The camp would be asleep, and the guards new at their posts.

decisions.choice: they had just posted the watchmen: the Midianites had only now changed guard
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis, with "only" before it: the new guards had only just been set. "They" are the Midianites. Fresh guards who did not yet know their surroundings, and the men just going off duty, would make the alarm all the greater.

decisions.choice: smashing: and they smashed
decisions.reason: The verb is in a form that simply names the action without person or tense; following "they blew", it continues the narrative: they blew and smashed.

decisions.choice: in the middle of the night, at the start of the second watch
decisions.reason: Readable explains the time and says that the middle of three watches is the second one.

source.text: וַֽ֠יִּתְקְעוּ שְׁלֹ֨שֶׁת הָרָאשִׁ֥ים בַּשּֽׁוֹפָרוֹת֮ וַיִּשְׁבְּר֣וּ הַכַּדִּים֒ וַיַּחֲזִ֤יקוּ בְיַד־שְׂמאוֹלָם֙בַּלַּפִּדִ֔ים וּבְיַ֨ד־יְמִינָ֔ם הַשּׁוֹפָר֖וֹת לִתְק֑וֹעַ וַֽיִּקְרְא֔וּ חֶ֥רֶב לַֽיהוָ֖ה וּלְגִדְעֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And blew [the] three [of] the companies on the trumpets, and they broke the jars, and they held in [the] hand of their left on the torches, and in [the] hand of their right the trumpets to blow; and they called out, a sword for Yahweh and for Gideon.

en.L: And the three companies blew on the trumpets and broke the jars, and they held the torches in their left hand and the trumpets in their right hand to blow; and they cried out, "A sword for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and for Gideon!"
en.B: All three companies blew their horns and broke their jars. With the torches in their left hands and the horns for blowing in their right, they shouted, "A sword for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and for Gideon!"
en.R: Then all three groups blew their trumpets and broke their jars. Each man had his torch in his left hand and his trumpet in his right, ready to blow. They all shouted, "A sword for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and for Gideon!"

sw.L: Navyo vikosi vitatu vikapiga baragumu, vikaivunja mitungi, wakashika mienge katika mkono wao wa kushoto, na baragumu katika mkono wao wa kuume ili kupiga; nao wakapiga kelele, "Upanga kwa ajili ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na kwa ajili ya Gideoni!"
sw.B: Vikosi vyote vitatu vilipiga baragumu na kuivunja mitungi yao. Wakiwa wameshika mienge katika mikono yao ya kushoto na baragumu za kupiga katika mikono yao ya kuume, walipiga kelele, "Upanga kwa ajili ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na kwa ajili ya Gideoni!"
sw.R: Kisha makundi yote matatu yalipiga baragumu na kuivunja mitungi yao. Kila mtu alishika mwenge wake katika mkono wa kushoto na baragumu yake katika mkono wa kulia, tayari kuipiga. Wote wakapiga kelele, "Upanga kwa ajili ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na kwa ajili ya Gideoni!"

es.L: Y las tres compañías tocaron los cuernos y quebraron los cántaros, y sostenían en su mano izquierda las antorchas, y en su mano derecha los cuernos para tocar; y gritaron: «¡Espada por {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} y por Gedeón!»
es.B: Las tres compañías tocaron sus cuernos y quebraron sus cántaros. Con las antorchas en la mano izquierda y los cuernos para tocar en la derecha, gritaron: «¡Espada por {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} y por Gedeón!»
es.R: Entonces los tres grupos tocaron sus cuernos y quebraron sus cántaros. Cada hombre tenía su antorcha en la mano izquierda y su cuerno en la derecha, listo para tocar. Todos gritaron: «¡Espada por {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} y por Gedeón!»

decisions.choice: A sword for the LORD and for Gideon: the sword fights on the LORD's behalf and on Gideon's
alternatives: The sword of the LORD and of Gideon!
decisions.reason: The cry has no verb: "a sword for the LORD and for Gideon". The word "for" marks those on whose behalf the sword is drawn, and to whom the victory will belong. It is also often understood as "the sword of the LORD and of Gideon", which comes to much the same; the Hebrew does not say "the" or "of".

decisions.choice: no sword in hand: the LORD's sword does the fighting
decisions.reason: Each man has a torch in one hand and a horn in the other, so no one is holding a sword. The cry echoes the Midianite's reading of the dream ("the sword of Gideon", verse 14), and in verse 22 it is the LORD who turns the enemy's swords against each other.

decisions.choice: they broke the jars: the torches blaze out at once
decisions.reason: Breaking the jars uncovered the torches in a single moment, so that 300 lights and 300 horns seemed to come from a great army on every side.

source.text: וַיַּֽעַמְדוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ תַּחְתָּ֔יו סָבִ֖יב לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה וַיָּ֧רָץ כָּל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֛ה וַיָּרִ֖יעוּ וַיָּנֽוּסוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they stood each in his place all around the camp; and ran all the camp, and they cried out, and they fled.

en.L: And they stood, each in his place, all around the camp; and all the camp ran, and they cried out and fled.
en.B: Each man stood in his place around the camp, while the whole Midianite army ran about, shouting, and fled.
en.R: Every Israelite stayed where he stood around the camp. The whole Midianite army began running and yelling and trying to get away.

sw.L: Nao wakasimama kila mmoja mahali pake kuizunguka kambi; nayo kambi yote ikakimbia, wakapiga yowe, wakatoroka.
sw.B: Kila mtu alisimama mahali pake kuizunguka kambi, huku jeshi lote la Midiani likikimbia huku na huko, likipiga kelele, likatoroka.
sw.R: Kila Mwisraeli alibaki pale aliposimama kuizunguka kambi. Jeshi lote la Wamidiani likaanza kukimbia na kupiga makelele na kujaribu kutoroka.

es.L: Y se quedaron, cada uno en su lugar, alrededor del campamento; y todo el campamento corrió, y gritaron y huyeron.
es.B: Cada hombre se quedó en su lugar alrededor del campamento, mientras todo el ejército madianita corría de un lado a otro gritando, y huía.
es.R: Cada israelita se quedó donde estaba, alrededor del campamento. Todo el ejército madianita comenzó a correr, a gritar y a tratar de escapar.

decisions.choice: they fled: the read form
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the Hebrew text could be read "they made [others] flee" or "they put to flight"; the form handed down for reading is "they fled", and the pinned data follows it. The sense is the same either way: the camp broke up in flight. Reviewers should check this against the manuscript notes.

decisions.choice: each stood in his place: Israel does not attack
decisions.reason: Gideon's men hold their positions; the enemy defeats itself. The victory is the LORD's, as verse 2 said it must be (compare Exodus 14:13-14).

decisions.choice: all the camp ran and cried out: the army in panic
decisions.reason: "The camp" is the army camped in it, as in verse 14. The verb for crying out is used for a shout of alarm or a war cry; here it is the cry of men in terror.

decisions.choice: Midianite (Balanced, Readable); Israelite (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew changes from Gideon's men to the enemy without naming either. Balanced and Readable add the names so that the reader can follow who is doing what.

source.text: וַֽיִּתְקְעוּ֮ שְׁלֹשׁ־מֵא֣וֹת הַשּׁוֹפָרוֹת֒ וַיָּ֣שֶׂם יְהוָ֗ה אֵ֣ת חֶ֥רֶב אִ֛ישׁ בְּרֵעֵ֖הוּ וּבְכָל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה וַיָּ֨נָס הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֜ה עַד־בֵּ֤ית הַשִּׁטָּה֙ צְֽרֵרָ֔תָה עַ֛ד שְׂפַת־אָבֵ֥ל מְחוֹלָ֖ה עַל־טַבָּֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And they blew, [the] three hundred, the trumpets, and set Yahweh [the] sword of each against his companion and in all the camp; and fled the camp as far as Beth-shittah toward Zererah, as far as [the] lip of Abel-meholah by Tabbath.

en.L: And the 300 blew the trumpets, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} set the sword of each man against his companion, and throughout the whole camp; and the camp fled as far as Beth-shittah toward Zererah, as far as the edge of Abel-meholah, by Tabbath.
en.B: When the 300 blew their horns, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} turned every man's sword against his comrade throughout the whole army. The army fled toward Zererah as far as Beth-shittah, and as far as the edge of Abel-meholah near Tabbath.
en.R: As the 300 men blew their trumpets, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made the Midianite soldiers attack one another with their swords all through the camp. The army ran away toward Zererah, as far as Beth-shittah, and on as far as the edge of Abel-meholah near Tabbath.

sw.L: Nao wale mia tatu wakapiga baragumu, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaugeuza upanga wa kila mtu juu ya mwenzake, katika kambi yote; nayo kambi ikakimbia mpaka Beth-shita kuelekea Zerera, mpaka ukingo wa Abel-mehola, karibu na Tabathi.
sw.B: Wale mia tatu walipopiga baragumu zao, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliugeuza upanga wa kila mtu juu ya mwenzake katika jeshi lote. Jeshi likakimbia kuelekea Zerera mpaka Beth-shita, na mpaka ukingo wa Abel-mehola karibu na Tabathi.
sw.R: Wale watu mia tatu walipokuwa wakipiga baragumu zao, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwafanya askari wa Midiani kushambuliana wao kwa wao kwa panga zao katika kambi yote. Jeshi likakimbia kuelekea Zerera, mpaka Beth-shita, na kuendelea mpaka ukingo wa Abel-mehola karibu na Tabathi.

es.L: Y tocaron los trescientos los cuernos, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} puso la espada de cada uno contra su compañero, y en todo el campamento; y el campamento huyó hasta Bet-sita, hacia Zerera, hasta el borde de Abel-mehola, junto a Tabat.
es.B: Cuando los trescientos tocaron sus cuernos, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} volvió la espada de cada uno contra su compañero en todo el ejército. El ejército huyó hacia Zerera hasta Bet-sita, y hasta el borde de Abel-mehola, cerca de Tabat.
es.R: Mientras los trescientos hombres tocaban sus cuernos, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} hizo que los soldados madianitas se atacaran unos a otros con sus espadas por todo el campamento. El ejército huyó hacia Zerera, hasta Bet-sita, y siguió hasta el borde de Abel-mehola, cerca de Tabat.

decisions.choice: the LORD set each man's sword against his companion: the enemy destroys itself
decisions.reason: In the dark and the panic the Midianites took each other for the enemy. The text says that the LORD brought this about. The same thing happens in other battles the LORD wins for Israel (1 Samuel 14:20; 2 Chronicles 20:23).

decisions.choice: Beth-shittah, Zererah, Abel-meholah, Tabbath: places on the way down to the Jordan
decisions.reason: The army fled east and south-east from the Valley of Jezreel toward the Jordan valley. Abel-meholah, later the home of Elisha (1 Kings 19:16), lay near the Jordan; the other places cannot be located with certainty.

decisions.choice: the edge: literally "the lip"
decisions.reason: The word for "lip" is used for an edge or border, as of the seashore in verse 12. Here it may mean the border of Abel-meholah's land, or the edge of the river near it.

decisions.choice: made the Midianite soldiers attack one another
decisions.reason: Readable names the Midianites and says plainly what "set each man's sword against his companion" means.

source.text: וַיִּצָּעֵ֧ק אִֽישׁ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל מִנַּפְתָּלִ֥י וּמִן־אָשֵׁ֖ר וּמִן־כָּל־מְנַשֶּׁ֑ה וַֽיִּרְדְּפ֖וּ אַחֲרֵ֥י מִדְיָֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And was called out [the] man of Israel from Naphtali and from Asher and from all Manasseh, and they pursued after Midian.

en.L: And the men of Israel were called out from Naphtali and from Asher and from all Manasseh, and they pursued after Midian.
en.B: Then the men of Israel from Naphtali, Asher and all Manasseh were called to arms, and they chased the Midianites.
en.R: Then men from the tribes of Naphtali, Asher and all of Manasseh were called out to fight, and they chased the Midianites.

sw.L: Nao watu wa Israeli wakaitwa kutoka Naftali, na kutoka Asheri, na kutoka Manase yote, wakawafuatia Midiani.
sw.B: Kisha watu wa Israeli kutoka Naftali, Asheri na Manase yote waliitwa kwenda vitani, wakawafuatia Wamidiani.
sw.R: Kisha watu kutoka makabila ya Naftali, Asheri na Manase yote waliitwa kwenda kupigana, wakawafukuza Wamidiani.

es.L: Y fueron convocados los hombres de Israel de Neftalí, de Aser y de todo Manasés, y persiguieron a Madián.
es.B: Entonces los hombres de Israel de Neftalí, de Aser y de todo Manasés fueron llamados a las armas, y persiguieron a los madianitas.
es.R: Entonces se llamó a pelear a los hombres de las tribus de Neftalí, de Aser y de todo Manasés, y persiguieron a los madianitas.

decisions.choice: the man of Israel: the men of Israel as one body
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses "man" in the singular for the fighting men of Israel taken together (as in 20:11).

decisions.choice: were called out: summoned to arms
decisions.reason: This form of the verb "cry out" means to be called together for battle (6:34-35; 12:1; 1 Samuel 13:4).

decisions.choice: Naphtali, Asher, Manasseh: tribes Gideon had called before
decisions.reason: These tribes, with Zebulun, had answered Gideon's first call (6:35). The men now called out probably include some of those he had just sent home (verses 7-8), joining in once the enemy was on the run.

decisions.choice: chased the Midianites
decisions.reason: "Midian" is the people; Balanced and Readable say "the Midianites".

source.text: וּמַלְאָכִ֡ים שָׁלַ֣ח גִּדְעוֹן֩ בְּכָל־הַ֨ר אֶפְרַ֜יִם לֵאמֹ֗ר רְד֞וּ לִקְרַ֤את מִדְיָן֙ וְלִכְד֤וּ לָהֶם֙ אֶת־הַמַּ֔יִם עַ֛ד בֵּ֥ית בָּרָ֖ה וְאֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן וַיִּצָּעֵ֞ק כָּל־אִ֤ישׁ אֶפְרַ֨יִם֙ וַיִּלְכְּד֣וּ אֶת־הַמַּ֔יִם עַ֛ד בֵּ֥ית בָּרָ֖ה וְאֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And messengers sent Gideon in all [the] hill country of Ephraim, saying, come down to meet Midian, and capture before them the waters as far as Beth-barah, and the Jordan. And was called out every man of Ephraim, and they captured the waters as far as Beth-barah, and the Jordan.

en.L: And Gideon sent messengers throughout all the hill country of Ephraim, saying, "Come down to meet Midian, and capture the waters ahead of them as far as Beth-barah, and the Jordan." And every man of Ephraim was called out, and they captured the waters as far as Beth-barah, and the Jordan.
en.B: Gideon sent messengers all through the hill country of Ephraim with this message: "Come down against the Midianites and take the waters ahead of them as far as Beth-barah, and the Jordan as well." So all the men of Ephraim were called out, and they took the waters as far as Beth-barah, and the Jordan.
en.R: Gideon sent messengers all through the hill country of Ephraim. They said, "Come down and fight the Midianites. Get to the river crossings before they do, as far as Beth-barah and the Jordan River." So all the men of Ephraim were called out. They took control of the river crossings as far as Beth-barah and the Jordan.

sw.L: Naye Gideoni akatuma wajumbe katika nchi yote ya milima ya Efraimu, akisema, "Shukeni kukutana na Midiani, mkayatwae maji mbele yao mpaka Beth-bara, na Yordani." Nao watu wote wa Efraimu wakaitwa, wakayatwaa maji mpaka Beth-bara, na Yordani.
sw.B: Gideoni alituma wajumbe katika nchi yote ya milima ya Efraimu na ujumbe huu: "Shukeni mkawashambulie Wamidiani, mkayashike maji mbele yao mpaka Beth-bara, na Yordani pia." Basi watu wote wa Efraimu waliitwa, wakayashika maji mpaka Beth-bara, na Yordani.
sw.R: Gideoni alituma wajumbe katika nchi yote ya milima ya Efraimu. Walisema, "Shukeni mkapigane na Wamidiani. Fikeni kwenye vivuko vya mto kabla yao, mpaka Beth-bara na Mto Yordani." Basi watu wote wa Efraimu waliitwa. Wakavishika vivuko vya mto mpaka Beth-bara na Yordani.

es.L: Y Gedeón envió mensajeros por toda la región montañosa de Efraín, diciendo: «{{plural_you:Desciendan|Descended}} al encuentro de Madián, y {{plural_you:tomen|tomad}} delante de ellos las aguas hasta Bet-bara, y el Jordán.» Y fueron convocados todos los hombres de Efraín, y tomaron las aguas hasta Bet-bara, y el Jordán.
es.B: Gedeón envió mensajeros por toda la región montañosa de Efraín con este mensaje: «{{plural_you:Bajen|Bajad}} contra los madianitas y {{plural_you:tómenles|tomadles}} la delantera en las aguas hasta Bet-bara, y también el Jordán.» Así que todos los hombres de Efraín fueron convocados, y tomaron las aguas hasta Bet-bara, y el Jordán.
es.R: Gedeón envió mensajeros por toda la región montañosa de Efraín. Decían: «{{plural_you:Bajen|Bajad}} y {{plural_you:peleen|pelead}} contra los madianitas. {{plural_you:Lleguen|Llegad}} antes que ellos a los vados del río, hasta Bet-bara y el río Jordán.» Así que todos los hombres de Efraín fueron convocados. Tomaron el control de los vados del río hasta Bet-bara y el Jordán.

decisions.choice: the waters: the streams and fords on the way to the Jordan
decisions.reason: To escape home, the Midianites had to cross the Jordan and the streams running down to it. Holding the fords cut off their escape, as Ehud's men did against Moab (3:28) and the Gileadites later against Ephraim (12:5-6).

decisions.choice: come down to meet Midian: come down against them
decisions.reason: "To meet" an enemy is to go out against him in battle (as in 20:25; 1 Samuel 4:1).

decisions.choice: and the Jordan: the Jordan as well
decisions.reason: "And the Jordan" is added after "as far as Beth-barah". It may mean the Jordan's own crossings besides the streams, or it may explain "the waters" as the Jordan itself. Either way the aim is to hold the river line.

decisions.choice: Ephraim: the tribe in the central hills
decisions.reason: Ephraim had not been called before (6:35). Its men come in now at the end, which leads to their complaint in 8:1.

decisions.choice: the river crossings
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the waters" were for in this battle: the places where the fleeing army could cross.

source.text: וַֽיִּלְכְּד֡וּ שְׁנֵֽי־שָׂרֵ֨י מִדְיָ֜ן אֶת־עֹרֵ֣ב וְאֶת־זְאֵ֗ב וַיַּהַרְג֨וּ אֶת־עוֹרֵ֤ב בְּצוּר־עוֹרֵב֙ וְאֶת־זְאֵב֙ הָרְג֣וּ בְיֶֽקֶב־זְאֵ֔ב וַֽיִּרְדְּפ֖וּ אֶל־מִדְיָ֑ן וְרֹאשׁ־עֹרֵ֣ב וּזְאֵ֔ב הֵבִ֨יאוּ֙ אֶל־גִּדְע֔וֹן מֵעֵ֖בֶר לַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And they captured [the] two commanders of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb; and they killed Oreb at [the] rock of Oreb, and Zeeb they killed at [the] winepress of Zeeb; and they pursued to Midian; and [the] head of Oreb and Zeeb they brought to Gideon from across the Jordan.

en.L: And they captured the two commanders of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb; and they killed Oreb at the rock of Oreb, and Zeeb they killed at the winepress of Zeeb; and they pursued Midian; and the head of Oreb and Zeeb they brought to Gideon from across the Jordan.
en.B: They also captured the two commanders of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb. Oreb they killed at the Rock of Oreb, and Zeeb at the Winepress of Zeeb. They kept up the pursuit of the Midianites, and they brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon from across the Jordan.
en.R: The men of Ephraim also captured two Midianite commanders named Oreb and Zeeb. They killed Oreb at the place called the Rock of Oreb and Zeeb at the place called the Winepress of Zeeb. They kept chasing the Midianites, and they brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon from the other side of the Jordan.

sw.L: Nao wakawakamata majemadari wawili wa Midiani, Orebu na Zeebu; wakamwua Orebu kwenye mwamba wa Orebu, na Zeebu wakamwua kwenye shinikizo la Zeebu; wakawafuatia Midiani; na vichwa vya Orebu na Zeebu wakamletea Gideoni kutoka ng'ambo ya Yordani.
sw.B: Pia waliwakamata majemadari wawili wa Midiani, Orebu na Zeebu. Orebu walimwua kwenye Mwamba wa Orebu, na Zeebu kwenye Shinikizo la Zeebu. Waliendelea kuwafuatia Wamidiani, nao wakamletea Gideoni vichwa vya Orebu na Zeebu kutoka ng'ambo ya Yordani.
sw.R: Watu wa Efraimu pia waliwakamata majemadari wawili wa Midiani walioitwa Orebu na Zeebu. Walimwua Orebu mahali paitwapo Mwamba wa Orebu, na Zeebu mahali paitwapo Shinikizo la Zeebu. Waliendelea kuwafukuza Wamidiani, nao wakamletea Gideoni vichwa vya Orebu na Zeebu kutoka ng'ambo ya Yordani.

es.L: Y capturaron a los dos jefes de Madián, Oreb y Zeeb; y mataron a Oreb en la peña de Oreb, y a Zeeb lo mataron en el lagar de Zeeb; y persiguieron a Madián; y trajeron la cabeza de Oreb y de Zeeb a Gedeón desde el otro lado del Jordán.
es.B: También capturaron a los dos jefes de Madián, Oreb y Zeeb. A Oreb lo mataron en la Peña de Oreb, y a Zeeb en el Lagar de Zeeb. Siguieron persiguiendo a los madianitas, y le llevaron a Gedeón las cabezas de Oreb y de Zeeb desde el otro lado del Jordán.
es.R: Los hombres de Efraín también capturaron a dos jefes madianitas llamados Oreb y Zeeb. Mataron a Oreb en el lugar llamado la Peña de Oreb, y a Zeeb en el lugar llamado el Lagar de Zeeb. Siguieron persiguiendo a los madianitas, y le llevaron a Gedeón las cabezas de Oreb y de Zeeb desde el otro lado del Jordán.

decisions.choice: Oreb and Zeeb: "raven" and "wolf"
decisions.reason: The two names mean "raven" and "wolf". The places where they died were known by their names, and later Scripture remembers their fall as a great act of the LORD (Isaiah 10:26; Psalm 83:12).

decisions.choice: the two commanders of Midian: army leaders, not the kings
decisions.reason: Oreb and Zeeb were leaders of the Midianite forces. The two kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna, escape across the Jordan and are pursued in chapter 8 (8:5, 10-12).

decisions.choice: from across the Jordan: the place of Gideon or of the heads is not certain
alternatives: to Gideon, who was across the Jordan
decisions.reason: The phrase may say where the heads came from, or where Gideon was when they reached him. The story of the crossing comes only in 8:4, so the narrator may be summing up the end of the pursuit here before going back to tell it. The wording is kept open at every level.

decisions.choice: the heads: proof that the enemy leaders were dead
decisions.reason: A victor brought back an enemy's head as proof of his death (1 Samuel 17:54; 31:9). The Hebrew has "head" in the singular, as a word for each of them.

decisions.choice: commanders
decisions.reason: The word often means "princes" or "officials"; in this military setting it is "commanders" at every level.

decisions.choice: The men of Ephraim
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "they"; verse 24 shows that the men of Ephraim are meant, and Readable names them.
